data.name: Auto-Block Cascade
data.description: Layered response playbooks: one indicator from any detection source, one FortiGuard verdict, and automatic blocking at every layer for a malicious verdict -- FortiGate at the gate, Defender on the endpoint, ThreatLocker's default-deny held closed by auto-rejecting matching approval requests -- reporting to ServiceNow (SIR) and Splunk. Clone before editing: this is a template collection, not a configuration.

workflows.name: >> Auto-Block Cascade > Resolve Indicator Verdict
workflows.description: Classifies an indicator and resolves its FortiGuard verdict (risk score, level, confidence, category). Referenced helper: pass it `indicator`; read the result off the calling step: verdict, indicator_type, defender_type, risk_score, risk_level, confidence, category.

groups.name: Note: Thresholds
groups.description:
FortiGuard risk score thresholds, 0-100. 80+ auto-enforces anywhere
that can carry the indicator; 50-79 stops for a human; below that the
cascade records only. One place to tune the autonomy.

groups.name: Note: Classify Indicator
groups.description:
Type sniffing without surprises: URL schemes first, then fixed-length
hex strings as file hashes, then dotted-quad IPv4, then IPv6 by colon,
then a domain. The Defender indicator vocabulary is derived alongside
because the endpoint layer needs it.

groups.name: Note: No Indicator
groups.description: The wrong entry is a dead end the caller can read, not an exception.

groups.name: Note: Search FortiGuard
groups.description:
One reputation answer for the indicator. The connector returns the
matched IOC rows; the first row carries the scored fields the verdict
reads (risk_score int, risk_level/confidence as {itemValue} picklists,
av_cate the category string).

groups.name: Note: Score Verdict
groups.description:
Type-safe scoring: the score arrives as a number or a string or
nothing at all; Python coerces once and the thresholds live in the
Thresholds step. Only string-coerced leaves are embedded (sandbox:
|tojson on a whole step result would hand Python lowercase `true`).

groups.name: Note: Verdict Out
groups.description:
The flat, primitive-only verdict bundle every caller reads off this
workflow_reference step (the last step's variables ARE the result).

workflows.name: >> Auto-Block Cascade > Enforce Indicator
workflows.description: The layered cascade: FortiGate blocklists, a Defender indicator block, auto-rejection of matching ThreatLocker approval requests -- then the ServiceNow SIR and Splunk records carrying every receipt. Referenced helper: pass it the verdict bundle from Resolve Indicator Verdict and an enforce flag.

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
Deployment-config values live here, the only step an operator should
need to touch: the FortiGate IPv4 Block Policy and the named IP group
a block lands in, and the Splunk KVStore app+collection that receives
every cascade record. The caller's `enforce` flag is normalized one
step later (Gate Layer Logic), where the reviewer can see it.

groups.name: Note: Gate Layer Logic
groups.description:
Normalize once more as plain booleans the when-guards can compare,
kept visible instead of buried in string comparisons everywhere.

groups.name: Note: Block URL At Gate
groups.description:
The web filter blocklist entry. FortiGate takes the URL or domain;
HTTPS SNI/FQDN matching is handled by the blocklist itself.

groups.name: Note: Block IPv4 At Gate
groups.description:
Policy-based IPv4 block into the named group/policy from
Configuration. Quarantine-based blocking is the connector's
alternative (ip_addresses + time_to_live); the group/policy form is
chosen because it persists and is visible in the blocklist.

groups.name: Note: Block IPv6 At Gate
groups.description:
The same block for IPv6 indicators: the option paths are kept as
separate steps so every param set is statically verifiable (a
templated ip_type hides which sub-params apply).

groups.name: Note: Defender Layer
groups.description: The endpoint block needs a Defender indicator type; hashes and network indicators both have one, anything else skips the layer.

groups.name: Note: Defender Indicator
groups.description:
'Alert and block': the indicator is blocked AND alerts on future hits, so
the SOC sees attempts already in flight. Defender keeps custom
indicators only while expirationTime is set; the tenant default
retention applies when blank.

groups.name: Note: ThreatLocker Try Switch
groups.description: The queue pull runs only for hashes, and only when enforcing.

groups.name: Note: Find Matching TL Requests
groups.description:
Recent approval queue rows; the match is the requester's own file
hash, exact, only when this indicator IS a file hash. The queue is
pulled with child organizations so a deny closes a request created
anywhere in the estate.

groups.name: Note: Match TL Requests
groups.description:
Exact hash equality, pending rows only (no actionDate): a request
that was already answered belongs to whoever answered it. The rows
are embedded as parallel strings-only lists (per-field extract,
string-coerced before |tojson) so a live response carrying booleans
cannot poison the sandbox with a lowercase true.

groups.name: Note: Reject Matching TL Requests
groups.description:
The auto-deny, with the verdict as the reason the user sees on the
toast follow-up and in their notification email. notify_on_response
true: the requestor must not discover the deny by trial and error.

groups.name: Note: Open SIR
Note: Record In Splunk
groups.description:
The SOC keeps their SIEM as their pane; the record lands where their
existing saved searches and Splunk Mobile alerting already look.
record_key = the indicator: blocking the same indicator twice
overwrites the record instead of duplicating it.

groups.name: Note: Cascade Summary
groups.description: The receipt bundle callers read back off the workflow_reference step.

workflows.name: Auto-Block Cascade > Block Indicator (API)
workflows.description: REST entry point of the layered response: POST /api/triggers/1/block-indicator with a JSON body: {"indicator": "...", "hostname": "...", "username": "...", "computer_id": "...", "source": "...", "notes": "..."}. Everything is optional except the indicator, so the cheapest detector integration is a one-field POST. Malicious verdicts auto-block at every layer; suspicious verdicts wait for a human; everything is reported to ServiceNow and Splunk. The raw body arrives at vars.steps.Start.input.params.api_body; this playbook parses it once and reads the fields defensively.

groups.name: Note: Parse Request
groups.description:
The body arrives at api_body as a parsed mapping or as a raw string,
depending on the sender; this normalizes both to a JSON text the
next step can read with from_json. (No code snippet here on
purpose: the sandbox disallows imports and API bodies need a JSON
parse, so the parse stays in Jinja where from_json is live-proven.)

groups.name: Note: Read Request
groups.description:
Field-per-var extraction; absent fields fall back so every
downstream step reads primitives.

groups.name: Note: Refuse Empty Request
groups.description: A malformed POST dies here with something the caller can read.

groups.name: Note: Resolve Verdict
groups.description:
The shared brain: classification + FortiGuard verdict, read back off
this step (verdict, indicator_type, defender_type, risk_score, ...).

groups.name: Note: Enforce Everywhere
groups.description:
The 3am path: no human required, every layer, then the SIR and
Splunk record.

Branch-safe receipt: the enforce lane and the record-only lane each
stamp the SAME var names immediately after the workflow_reference,
so the shared Done step below never references a step that only
ran on a sibling branch.

workflows.name: Auto-Block Cascade > ThreatLocker Request Autotriage
workflows.description: Pulls the ThreatLocker approval queue, verdicts the next pending request's file hash with FortiGuard, auto-rejects it with the verdict as the reason when malicious, and cascades the hash to the other layers. Not-malicious requests become a human task. Run it from the Run button or a schedule.

groups.name: Note: Pick Next Untriaged
groups.description:
One request per run: pending only (no actionDate), hash present. The
connector's shipped Decide Elevation Request sample is the
multi-choice human surface; this is the overnight half, so it stays
narrow and one-at-a-time. Rows embed as parallel strings-only lists
(per-field extract, string-coerced before |tojson) so live DTO
booleans cannot reach the sandbox as bare `true`.

groups.name: Note: Nothing To Triage
groups.description: The quiet case is a result too: nothing malicious was waiting.

groups.name: Note: Reject Request
groups.description:
The user sees this reason on the request's response and in the
notification; the verdict is not a mystery to them.

groups.name: Note: Cascade The Hash
groups.description:
Defender IOC + the SIR/Splunk records (the gate carries hashes for
no one; ThreatLocker-side this run already closed the request, and
the endpoint default-deny was never opened).

groups.name: Note: Human Queue
groups.description:
Suspicious, clean or unknown: a human decides -- with the connector's
Decide Elevation Request playbook as the natural next step, since it
loads the permit context and the decision history.

workflows.name: Auto-Block Cascade > Darktrace Breach Sweep
workflows.description: Pulls Darktrace model breaches from a lookback window and feeds the first one's destination indicators into the layered response (verdict first; malicious cascades, anything less records with a task). Run it from the Run button or a schedule.

arguments.outcome: Darktrace sweep: no model breaches in the window ({{ vars.lookback_minutes }} minutes).

params.python_function:
cands = [
    {{ (vars.steps.Get_Breach_Details.data.externalhost_1 | default('', true)) | string | tojson }},
    {{ (vars.steps.Get_Breach_Details.data.externalip_1 | default('', true)) | string | tojson }},
    {{ (vars.steps.Get_Breach_Details.data.externalhost | default('', true)) | string | tojson }},
    {{ (vars.steps.Get_Breach_Details.data.externalip | default('', true)) | string | tojson }},
    {{ (vars.steps.Get_Breach_Details.data.external_endpoint | default('', true)) | string | tojson }},
]
out = []
i = 0
while i < len(cands):
    v = str(cands[i]).strip()
    if v != '' and v not in out:
        out.append(v)
    i = i + 1
picked = ''
j = 0
while j < len(out):
    cand = out[j]
    looks_ip = True
    parts = cand.split('.')
    if len(parts) != 4:
        looks_ip = False
    p = 0
    while p < len(parts):
        try:
            q = int(parts[p])
        except Exception:
            looks_ip = False
            break
        if q < 0 or q > 255:
            looks_ip = False
            break
        p = p + 1
    if looks_ip or ('.' in cand and ' ' not in cand):
        picked = cand
        break
    j = j + 1
print({'candidates': out, 'picked': picked})

arguments.outcome: Darktrace sweep: nothing actionable in the window ({{ vars.lookback_minutes }} minutes). Candidates seen: {{ vars.steps.Extract_Indicators.data.code_output.candidates | default([], true) | join(', ') | default('none', true) }}.

groups.name: Note: Configuration
groups.description:
Darktrace takes epoch seconds for its window. Acknowledged breaches
are skipped by default -- acknowledged means a human already chose
a lane.

groups.name: Note: Quiet Window Result
groups.description:
Terminal for the no-breach branch; it deliberately reads no
breach-detail data (those steps did not run on this branch, and a
reference here would be branch-unsafe).

groups.name: Note: Get Breach Details
groups.description:
The breach detail payload carries the endpoint, hostname and
destination fields (model-dependent -- the candidate keys are read
defensively; a renamed key costs a missed candidate, never a crash).

groups.name: Note: Extract Indicators
groups.description:
Candidate values come from the known destination keys, each
string-coerced before |tojson (whole-payload embedding would hand
Python lowercase true/false the moment a live detail carries a
boolean). The FIRST candidate that looks like an IP or a dotted
hostname is swept this run; the SIR/task record keeps the whole
candidate list.

groups.name: Note: Stamp Enforce Receipt
groups.description:
Branch-safe receipt: the enforce lane and the task lane each stamp
the SAME var names, so the shared Sweep Summary never references a
step that only ran on a sibling branch.

groups.name: Note: Record Breach Indicator
Note: Stamp Task Receipt
groups.description: The task lane's copy of the same receipt vars -- no SIR exists on this lane.
